logp.method_description: Partition coefficients for the platinum complexes were determined in triplicate in an n-octanol/water system, with different ratios (1:1, 1:2, 2:1). Each complex was dissolved in n-octanol at the concentrations 16.7, 12.5, or 10 μM and subsequently, an appropriate volume of water was added. The mixtures were shaken mechanically for 1 h to ensure the distribution between the two solvent phases. The samples were then centrifuged (13,000 rpm, 10 min). Afterwards, the platinum concentration was determined in the octanol phases by UV–vis spectrophotometry, after collecting a calibration line for each complex. Results are expressed as the logarithm of the partition coefficient of octanol/water (log Po/w), which is the logarithm of the concentration of platinum in the n-octanol divided by its concentration in the aqueous layer.
